subject.title: Feature: Per-call cost tracking & auth profile attribution

question: Should OpenClaw make resolved auth-profile attribution part of the canonical completed-model-call accounting contract, and which surfaces may expose it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix affects privacy, billing metadata, transcripts, gateway APIs, diagnostics, plugin contracts, and UI/status behavior, so automation should not choose the exposure boundary.

options.title: Design canonical attribution contract
options.body: Record resolved authProfileId and cost at the normalized completed-call seam, expose redacted/additive readers, and make this the source for status, usage, diagnostics, and plugin views.

options.title: Limit to plugin or diagnostics first
options.body: Keep native status/usage unchanged for now and expose safe usage metadata through an explicit maintainer-approved plugin observer capability.

options.title: Defer native attribution
options.body: Keep current provider/model cost summaries and external workarounds until maintainers are ready to design credential-adjacent accounting metadata.

recommendation.title: Design canonical attribution contract
recommendation.body: Record resolved authProfileId and cost at the normalized completed-call seam, expose redacted/additive readers, and make this the source for status, usage, diagnostics, and plugin views.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest history on current usage-cost summaries and prior review of this exact issue.
